description: A competing tool (markitdown's audio route, speech_recognition.recognize_google) uploaded a user's audio to a third party with nothing in the interface saying so. This eval exists to guarantee that transcribe.py's automatic path can never do that: `resolve("auto")` must never produce a network backend, and any network backend (groq, openai) must disclose provider/endpoint/duration/cost before anything is sent, and only ever because the caller named it explicitly. Cases 1-8 below are argv-driven, run against the real CLI via subprocess, and are asserted by grade.py's `check()`. Two things below are NOT here, by design: (a) cases 9-13 -- the backend-registry matrix across six OS/arch pairs, the parakeet has_whisper_metrics exception, and estimate_cost's None-for-local contract -- live directly in grade.py as pure-Python assertions against tslib.backends, since they take no argv and need no subprocess; (b) case 7, a malformed `--replace` pair, is NOT run through the CLI: transcribe.py validates --replace pairs (corrections.build) only AFTER decoding, which this suite cannot reach offline (no ASR library, no network, no model download), so it is instead asserted as a direct call to tslib.corrections.build() in grade.py, with the reason recorded there and in this file. All argv cases that touch a real file additionally require ffmpeg/ffprobe on PATH (transcribe.py checks for both unconditionally before resolving a backend) -- grade.py detects their absence and SKIPs those cases rather than failing.
